title: What can you say about sodium in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for sodium; the strongest is "As part of a carbohydrate-electrolyte drink, helps maintain endurance performance during prolonged endurance exercise" (moderate, 20-50 mmol sodium per litre of drink a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Prevents or treats dehydration from diarrhea or vomiting".

supported_wordings.wording: As part of a carbohydrate-electrolyte drink, helps maintain endurance performance during prolonged endurance exercise.
supported_wordings.why: Authorized in the EU after EFSA review for drinks of a set composition; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: 20-50 mmol sodium per litre of drink a day
supported_wordings.dose_details: A concentration in the prepared drink, not a daily amount: 20-50 mmol of sodium per litre (460-1,150 mg per litre). The EU sets the whole formula: 80-350 kcal per litre from carbohydrates, at least 75% of that energy from high-glycaemic carbohydrates such as glucose, glucose polymers and sucrose, and an osmolality of 200-330 mOsm/kg water.
supported_wordings.form: A carbohydrate-electrolyte drink that meets the EU conditions; not sodium on its own

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Prevents or treats dehydration from diarrhea or vomiting
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease state; Health Canada ties its oral rehydration uses to acute gastroenteritis (Canada only notes).

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Works like an IV drip, or IV-level hydration
wordings_to_avoid.why: Compares the product to intravenous fluids, a medical treatment.
Names a medical emergency; no listed source supports it.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
